note: Independently re-judged against committed source 71b1f3d799; the unrelated working-tree checker rewrites were excluded. RFC 7606 Section 5.1: "Since older BGP speakers may not implement these restrictions, an implementation MUST still be prepared to receive these fields in any position or combination." The single-positive-polarity annotation is appropriate: rejecting these otherwise valid shapes solely for the sender restrictions would violate the receiver obligation. TestRFC7606MPReachIPv4NextHopValid and the four TestRFC7606Section51Accepts* units require the exact RFC7606ActionNone for MP_REACH/MP_UNREACH after earlier attributes, distinct MP attributes together and each MP attribute with legacy NLRI. Their complete attribute lengths and mandatory ORIGIN/AS_PATH/NEXT_HOP inputs isolate receiver tolerance from syntax or missing-attribute errors. ValidateUpdateRFC7606Peer walks each framed attribute, treats the two MP codes separately and rejects repeated occurrences of the same MP code, while Session.classifyRFC7606 locates the legacy withdrawn, attribute and reachable sections independently; Session.applyRFC7606 returns the clean UPDATE for ActionNone. The receive-combinations functional carrier seeds all withdrawal owners and requires a receiver acknowledgement before the mixed inputs, then checks every expected output component in its current sequence group. The relay-one-field carrier similarly seeds and acknowledges the withdrawn route, requires the withdrawal and announcement output and rejects UPDATE-error NOTIFICATION logging. Those daemon assertions fail if a tested mixed input is dropped, reset or stripped. The committed checkRFC7606MixedUpdate retains replay liveness, client AS_PATH, mixed announcement, withdrawn-prefix and live-FRR-session checks; assertion 6 now additionally requires the exact selected, installed BGP prefix with the injector next hop active and in the FIB in that same native zebra entry through requireRouteInstalledVia. FRR vty_show_ip_route and nexthop_json_helper produce those route and hop state fields. The interop carrier corroborates accepted delivery/installation; it does not independently prove split-versus-unsplit wire encoding, and its unseeded withdrawn-prefix absence is not credited as withdrawal delivery. The functional seeded cases provide that distinction. The same receiver-tolerance claim remains enforced with stronger installation proof. This is a source rejudgment, with no new runtime or mutation result claimed.
